title: Connective hypercohomology on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i<0$. Write $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ for global sections derived on K-injective resolutions, and $H^0(\mathcal C,E)=H^0R\Gamma(\mathcal C,E)$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. The canonical map induced by $\mathcal H^0(E)[0]\to E$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal H^0(E))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(\mathcal C,E).$$
Moreover $H^iR\Gamma(\mathcal C,E)=0$ for $i<0$. The same assertions hold on each localized ringed site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and the isomorphisms commute with restriction in $U$. If $E=Q(P^\bullet)$ for a complex zero in negative degrees, this identifies $H^0(\mathcal C,E)$ with $\ker(\Gamma(\mathcal C,P^0)\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,P^1))$. These identifications are natural in $E$. For a morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\mathcal C',\mathcal O')\to(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], when also $Lf^*E$ has no negative cohomology, they identify pullback on hypercohomology with the map on sections induced by $\mathcal H^0(E)\to f_*\mathcal H^0(Lf^*E)$ coming from the derived adjunction unit $E\to Rf_*Lf^*E$. Derived tensor pullback uses K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. No upper cohomological bound is imposed.

source.place: Tag 071J, section-derived-functors, resolution functor and derived evaluation; Tag 07A5, section-unbounded, comparison with K-injective derived sections. The connective degree-zero consequence used in quot.tex Tag 08JX, first sentence of the proof.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], $\mathcal A$ is abelian with enough injectives. The assumed lower cohomological bound puts $E$ in $D^+(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] with $n=0$: choose a complex $I$ of injectives with $I^r=0$ for $r<0$ and $\alpha:QI\cong E$. It is K-injective, also for the unbounded category. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] every complex has a K-injective resolution, so [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] applies to the additive global-section and evaluation functors on all of $D(\mathcal O)$, and computes them on this $I$ by applying the functors termwise. There is no upper bound on $I$.

Set $Z=\ker(d_I^0:I^0\to I^1)$. Since $I^{-1}=0$, [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] identifies $Z$ with $\mathcal H^0(QI)$. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Global sections also preserve this kernel: a morphism $\mathcal O\to I^0$ factors through $Z$ exactly when its composite with $d_I^0$ is zero. Hence
$$\Gamma(\mathcal C,Z)=\ker(\Gamma(\mathcal C,I^0)\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,I^1))=H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal C,I)).$$
There are no degree-zero boundaries and all negative terms of this section complex vanish. Thus [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives negative cohomology zero, and [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] and $\alpha$ give the required degree-zero isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 071J (section-derived-functors), 07A5 (section-unbounded); quot.tex Tag 08JX (lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex), opening proof sentence

proof.text: The isomorphism just obtained has the asserted normalization. The canonical truncation map $\mathcal H^0(QI)[0]\to QI$ is represented by $Z[0]\hookrightarrow I$: this is the explicit truncation complex of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Write $\eta$ for the derived-global-section unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Apply its naturality to $Z[0]\hookrightarrow I$. On $I$, $\eta_I$ is invertible, so the map from ordinary sections of $Z$ into $H^0R\Gamma(QI)$ is the map induced by inclusion of the same zero-cycles into $\Gamma(I)$. It is exactly the isomorphism in step 2. Applying step 2 to the degree-zero sheaf $Z[0]$ identifies its derived degree zero with $\Gamma(Z)$, so this also verifies that the map is the one induced by the canonical derived truncation arrow, then transported by $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 05RR (section-derived-categories), standard truncations; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 071J (section-derived-functors), R^0F=F

proof.text: For two such models $QI\cong E$, $QJ\cong E'$ and a derived map $v:E\to E'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents the transported map by $a:I\to J$, uniquely up to homotopy. The unit naturality of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computes its derived-section map by $\Gamma(a)$. Both the cohomology-sheaf map and the section-complex map send a zero-cycle $s$ to $a^0(s)$. They therefore give the same map under step 2. If $a,b$ are homotopic, [def-pur-kinjective-complex] gives $a^0-b^0=d_J^{-1}h^0+h^1d_I^0$, which vanishes on $\ker d_I^0$ because $J^{-1}=0$. This proves naturality and, taking $v=1_E$ between two models, independence of choices.

For every object $U$, restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], so it identifies $\mathcal H^0(E)|_U$ with $\mathcal H^0(E|_U)$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $I|_U$ is K-injective; it is zero in negative degrees. The sectionwise formula of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives $\Gamma(\mathcal C/U,I|_U)=I(U)$. Thus the same calculation in step 2 computes derived sections on the slice and identifies its degree zero with $\ker(I^0(U)\to I^1(U))$. For $a:V\to U$, the actual restriction chain map sends a cycle $s$ to $s|_V$. Both kernel identifications have that same formula. The derived restriction is computed by this chain map, by the derived-unit equation [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] on these K-injective representatives. Hence the isomorphisms commute with restriction for every arrow, including iterated localization.

If $P^r=0$ for $r<0$, then $\mathcal H^0(QP)=\ker(d_P^0:P^0\to P^1)$ by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Applying $\Gamma=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O,-)$ to this kernel gives precisely $\ker(\Gamma(P^0)\to\Gamma(P^1))$, by the factorization property of a kernel and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Compose this equality with steps 2 and 3. The construction sends a section cycle to its own degree-zero cohomology class under the derived-section unit, and step 4 proves its naturality. This does not assert that ordinary sections of $P$ compute higher hypercohomology.

source.place: Tag 071J (section-derived-functors); quot.tex Tag 08JX (lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex), connective degree-zero calculation

proof.text:
Put $F=Lf^*E$, assumed connective. Use the canonical derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and represent $F$ by a nonnegative K-injective $J$ as in step 1. Then $Rf_*F=Q(f_*J)$ by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Since $f_*$ is a right adjoint on modules [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], it preserves kernels: maps into a kernel correspond under the adjunction to maps whose composite with its defining arrow is zero. Consequently $f_*J$ has zero negative terms and
$$\mathcal H^0(Rf_*F)=\ker(f_*d_J^0)=f_*\ker(d_J^0)=f_*\mathcal H^0(F).$$
Apply steps 2--4 to the derived unit $u:E\to Rf_*F$. They identify $H^0R\Gamma(u)$ with sections of $\mathcal H^0(u)$ under this kernel equality. Finally the derived direct-image composition of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied also to the global-section ringed morphism from $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ to the point with ring $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, identifies $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,Rf_*F)$ with $R\Gamma(\mathcal C',F)$ (forget scalars). In degree zero its normalized resolution map is ordinary $\Gamma(\mathcal C,f_*\ker d_J^0)=\Gamma(\mathcal C',\ker d_J^0)$: the resolution map on $f_*J$ induces its cohomology map, and steps 2--4 identify that map with the same kernel sections. Thus pullback, defined by this derived unit followed by the composition comparison, is exactly the section map stated in the item. K-flat resolutions enter only to define $Lf^*$; neither $E$ nor $F$ needs an upper bound.

Step 1 builds a nonnegative injective K-injective model from the D^+ representative (n=0); prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist makes RΓ defined and η_I invertible. Step 2: since I^{-1}=0, H^0=ker d^0, Γ=Hom(O,-) preserves the kernel, and H^{<0}Γ(I)=0. Step 3: the τ_{≤0} subcomplex is Z[0], and η-naturality shows the map is canonical. Step 4: homotopies vanish on ker d^0 because J^{-1}=0. Step 6 gives ker(ΓP^0→ΓP^1) without claiming anything about higher cohomology. Step 7: f_* is a right adjoint, so H^0Rf_*F=f_*H^0F; the global-section morphism to the point together with the κ normalization (resolution j:f_*J→J', which may be chosen nonnegative) gives Γ(C,f_*H^0F)=Γ(C',H^0F).
